insights.insight: Ad tech sells probabilistic purchase inference at $5–$150 CPA; this protocol settles verified purchase events at ~$0.10 per receipt — a 50–200x cost delta that isn't incremental improvement, it's a different category of signal entirely.

Etsy's entry into the top brand list marks the first digital-native marketplace in the dataset, confirming the protocol has moved beyond physical retail receipts into purchase confirmation emails — the natural expansion path for DKIM-based verification.

6,792 cryptographically verified receipts across 14 CBSAs and growing brand diversity create a network effect where each new receipt increases the signal value of all prior receipts — a dataset that cannot be replicated without rebuilding the network from scratch.

A single cycle added 19 new CBSAs (86.4% diffusion rate), including Chicago, Philadelphia, and San Francisco, following a complete quiet cycle — the expansion is non-linear and concentrated, meaning geographic coverage can shift materially in a single heartbeat.

Raw throughput velocity has been below 1.0x for 11+ consecutive cycles while acceleration holds above 1.0x — the 7-day GMV window jumped to $36,436 (+$4,075 in one cycle), consistent with compounding momentum beneath suppressed surface numbers.

insights.topic: Brand category drift toward specialty and digital
insights.insight: The top brand list has shifted from big-box anchors (Walmart, Home Depot) toward specialty retail (Whole Foods, Total Wine) and now online marketplaces (Etsy), signaling that verified commerce data is tracking higher-intent, higher-margin purchase categories.
